summary: The root جَذَا (jadhā) primarily means to stand firmly or remain fixed, like a tick clinging to a camel or a stone supporting a pot.
lane: 1 جَذَا ذ , (S, K,) aor. جَذُوَ , (TA,) inf. n. جَذْوٌ and جُذُوٌّ , (K,) It (a thing, TA) stood firmly; as also . (S, K.) You say also, جَذَا عَلَى شَىْءٍ He [or it, for instance, a stone of those (three in number) upon which a cooking-pot is places, as is implied in the S, (see جَاذٍ ,)] remained firm upon a thing. (S.) And جَذَا القُرَادُ فِى جَنْبِ البَعِير The ticks stuck, and clave, to the side of the camel: (ISd, K, TA:) and جذا بِالجَمَلِ clung to the camel. (TA.) -b2- I. q. جَثًا [ He sat upon his knees; &c.]; (AA, Fr, S, K;) as also , [in form] like اِرْعَوَى ; (TA;) except that جذا is more indicative of keeping to a place: (Kh, TA:) or he stood upon the extremities of his toes: (As, K:) accord. to Th, جُذُوٌّ is [the standing ] upon the extremities of the toes; and جُثُوٌّ is [the sitting] upon the knees: (TA:) and accord. to IAar, means [a man standing ] upon his feet; and جَاثٍ , [one sitting] upon his knees. (S, TA.) Accord. to El-Hasan Ibn-'AbdAllah El-Kátib El-Isbahánee, جَذَا , inf. n. جُذُوٌّ , said of a bird, means He stood upon the extremities of his toes, and warbled, and went round in his warbling; which he does only when seeking the female: and said of a horse, it means he stood upon his toes; and in like manner when said of a man, whether for dancing or for some other purpose. (TA.) A poet says, (S,) namely, En-Noamán Ibn-Nadleh, (TA,) إِذَا شِئْتُ غَنَّتْنِى دَهَاقِينُ قَرْيَةٍ وَصَنَّاجَةٌ تَجْذُو عَلَى حَرْفِ مَنْسِمِ [ When I will, the husbandmen of a village sing to me, and a female player with the cymbals, standing upon the extremity of a toe ]. (S, TA: but in the latter, عَلَى كُلِّ مَنْسِمِ [ upon every toe ].) -b3- Also, inf. n. جُذُوٌّ , He, or it, was, or became, erect, and straight; (TA;) and so , inf. n. اِجْذِيذَآءٌ . (Az, TA.) See جَوَاذِ as applied to she-camels, in two places, voce جَاذٍ . -b4- It (a camel's hump) bore fat [ so that it became elevated ]. (K.) -b5- جَذَا مَنْخِرَاهُ His nostrils were, or became, raised and extended. (TA.) -b6- Er-Rá'ee, describing a strong, or sturdy, she-camel, says, لَمْ يَجْذُ مِرْفَقُهَا فِى الدَّفِ مِنْ زَوَرِ meaning Her elbow did not stand out far from the side by reason of [ the distortion termed ] زَوَر . (TA.)

headwords.def: (S, K,) aor. جَ ُوَ, (TA,) inf. n. جَ ْوٌ and جُ ُوٌّ, (K,) It (a thing, TA) stood firmly; as also. (S, K.) You say also, جَ َا عَلَى شَىْءٍ He [or it, for instance, a stone of those (three in number) upon which a cooking-pot is places, as is implied in the S, (see جَا ٍ,)] remained firm upon a thing. (S.) And جَ َا القُرَادُ فِى جَنْبِ البَعِير The ticks stuck, and clave, to the side of the camel: (ISd, K, TA:) and ج ا بِالجَمَلِ clung to the camel. (TA.) I. q.

: see 1, first sentence. Also He (a young camel) bore fat in his hump. (Ks, S, K.) El-Khansà says, يُجْ ِينَ نَيًّا وَلَا يجْ ِينَ قِرْدَانَا They bear fat [ in their humps ], and have not ticks clinging to them. (IB, TA.) He lifted a stone, (AA, S, TA,) in order that he might know thereby his strength. (TA.) One says, هُمْ يُجْ ُونَ حَجَرًا [ They lift a stone, in order to prove their strength, and vie, one with another, in lifting it, for that purpose ].

and جُ ْوَةٌ and جَ ْوَةٌ (S, Msb, K) [ A brand, or fire-brand; ] i. q. جِ ْمَةٌ, (AO, S, K,) i. e. a thick piece of wood, having fire at the end of it or not: (AO, S, in explanation of the first:) or a thick piece of fire-wood, not flaming: (AO, TA, in explanation of جِ ْوَةٌ مِنَ النَّارِ:) or a thick stick, one end of which is a live coal: (Aboo-Sa'eed, TA:) or a thick stick upon which fire is taken [ by kindling one end ]: (ISk, TA:) and a piece ( قَبْسَةٌ, K, or قِطْعَةٌ, Har p.

[part. n. of 1; fem. جَا ِيَةٌ: pl. masc. جِ َآءٌ; pl. fem. جَا ِيَاتٌ and جَوَا ٍ ]. A rájiz says, (S,) namely, 'Amr Ibn-Jebel-El-Asadee, (TA,) لَمْ يُبْقِ مِنْهَا سَبَلُ الرَّ َا ِ غَيْرَ أَثَافِى مِرْجَلٍ جَوَا ِى i. e. [ The continual fine rain left not thereof save the three stones that were the supports of a cooking-pot ] remaining firm. (S, TA.) I. q.

[act. part. n. of 4]. مِثْلُ الأَرْزَةِ المُجْ ِيَةِ عَلَى الأَرْضِ, (S,) or كَالأَرْزَةِ المج ية على وَجْهِ الارض, (TA,) occurring in a trad., (S, TA,) describing the unbeliever, (TA,) means [ Like the pine-tree ] that is firm (S, TA) and erect [ upon the ground ]. (TA.)

[in the CK, erroneously, المَجْ ُوْ ِىُّ,] Keeping constantly to the dwelling, or to the camel's saddle and the dwelling, ( الرَّحْل and المَنْزِل, AA, S, K,) not quitting it: (AA, S:) like مُجْ َوْ ٍ عَلَى الرَّحْلِ. (AA, S) And A man who lowers, or abases, himself; (El-Hejeree, ISd, TA;) as though he clave to the ground by reason of his abjectness; from جَ َا القُرَادُ فِى جَنْبِ البَعِيرِ [q. v.]. (ISd, TA.)

headword_note: Lane organises by verb form and principal noun, not by every inflected form. A word with no headword entry falls back to the root meaning; nothing is inferred.
